Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Claims Handling Standards Manual and the 50-state Unfair Claims Requirement Matrix; escalation to the Chief Claims Officer for operational conflicts and to Regulatory Counsel for interpretation

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — NAIC Model 900 Sections 4 (file and record documentation), 6 (failure to acknowledge), 7 (prompt investigation), 8 (fair and equitable settlement) and 9-10 (auto and fire/property), re-read at each annual review against each state's own adoption; representative text is Alabama Ala. Code 27-12-24 and Ala. Admin. Code r. 482-1-125, with Arkansas and Arizona adoptions of Model 900 confirmed on the same pass

In-scope processes.value: The end-to-end claim lifecycle governed by Model 900: FNOL intake, written acknowledgement, assignment and prompt investigation, 45-day status updates, coverage accept/deny decision, settlement negotiation, payment issue, denial with stated basis, reopen and closure — for auto, property, liability, life and disability claims in all 50 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: ClaimCenter holds the per-state acknowledgement, status-letter and accept/deny SLA clocks, the diary rules and the approved correspondence templates that carry the written standard into the adjuster desktop; the approved manual itself is versioned in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Claims Handling Standards Manual (CHS-900) plus its appendix, the 50-state Unfair Claims Requirement Matrix, which carries per state: acknowledgement day count and business-vs-calendar basis, status-letter interval, accept/deny day count from proof of loss, payment day count from settlement agreement, required denial-letter content and DOI contact block, and the claim-file documentation minimum

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved jointly by the Chief Claims Officer (operational feasibility) and the Head of Compliance (regulatory sufficiency) after Regulatory Counsel legal review; full re-approval each year by March 31, plus an out-of-cycle amendment within 30 days of any state bulletin, statute amendment or market conduct exam finding that changes a day count or letter requirement

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual review must close with signed approval by March 31 each year; each state bulletin or regulation change opens a 30-day matrix-amendment clock; ClaimCenter configuration must reflect an approved amendment within 45 days of approval; attestation training is assigned within 15 days of publication

Deadline reminders configured.value: Control calendar entries in the GRC platform fire at T-60, T-30 and T-7 days to the March 31 approval date to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager, and a same-day alert to the regulatory-change queue whenever a monitored state bulletin feed posts a claims-practices item

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Every approved version of CHS-900 and the state matrix, its redline, the counsel review memo, the dual approval signatures and the training completion extract are retained 7 years from supersession in the compliance evidence repository — longer than the 5-year look-back a market conduct examiner typically applies to claim practice

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any state whose matrix row is stale past the 30-day bulletin clock, any ClaimCenter clock that does not match the approved matrix, and any missed March 31 approval is logged as a procedure-currency exception with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every procedure-currency exception and every out-of-cycle amendment made in response to a bulletin or exam finding

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All 50 jurisdiction rows of the Unfair Claims Requirement Matrix plus every section of CHS-900 in force during the test year, together with the corresponding ClaimCenter SLA and letter-template configuration records

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on day counts — any state row whose acknowledgement, status-interval, accept/deny or payment day count differs from the current state text is a fail; any ClaimCenter clock that does not match its approved matrix row is a fail; missing the March 31 approval date is an automatic fail regardless of content quality

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is an annual review with 30-day bulletin amendments; the test runs annually in Q2 immediately after the March 31 approval, with a mid-year spot check of the bulletin-amendment log so a 30-day breach is caught inside the same year

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Auditor must not have drafted, edited or approved any sampled matrix row or CHS-900 section

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual CHS-900 currency workpaper — matrix extract, dated state-text captures, ClaimCenter configuration export, re-performance notes and the exception schedule — filed in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Claims Practices / <year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Approved CHS-900 PDF with the state matrix appendix, version history, approval signature page and training completion roster, producible for an examiner's procedure request within 5 business days of a call letter

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance owns delivery of the procedures to the examiner-in-charge through the exam portal; Regulatory Counsel clears any statement about how the standard was applied before it leaves the building

checklist.step: Open the annual review and lock the baseline version
actions: In the compliance evidence repository open Market Conduct / Claims Practices and check out the current approved CHS-900 manual and its Unfair Claims Requirement Matrix appendix.
Record the baseline version number, approval date and approver names on the review cover sheet, then create the working draft as version n+1 with change tracking on.
Ask the Chief Claims Officer's office for the list of claim organisations, lines and jurisdictions in force so no writing company or state is reviewed out of scope.
Open a review control record in the GRC platform with the March 31 approval date as the due date and the Head of Compliance as approver.
checklist.done: the working draft, its baseline reference and a dated GRC review control record with a March 31 due date all exist.

checklist.step: Refresh the 50-state unfair claims requirement matrix from primary text
actions: For each of the 50 jurisdictions open the state's own unfair claims settlement practices act and implementing regulation (representative: Ala. Code 27-12-24 and Ala. Admin. Code r. 482-1-125; Arkansas and Arizona adoptions of NAIC Model 900).

Read and record on the state row: acknowledgement day count and whether the count is calendar or working days, the status-update interval, the accept/deny day count measured from receipt of proof of loss, the payment day count from settlement agreement, and any state-specific denial-letter content.
Paste the exact quoted sentence and the section cite next to each day count — never a paraphrase.
Save a dated PDF capture of each state's text as <state>-ucspa-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf into the review folder as the evidence behind the row.
Flag rows where the state exceeds Model 900 (shorter clocks, extra notices, mandatory DOI contact language) so the manual states the stricter rule as the operating standard.
checklist.done: all 50 rows carry quoted text, a section cite and a dated capture, with stricter-than-model rules flagged.

checklist.step: Sweep the year's bulletins, enforcement actions and exam reports for changes
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System filter the regulatory-change queue to Category = Market Conduct / Claims and Received date inside the last 12 months.

Add to the sweep each DOI bulletin page for the jurisdictions where the company writes, plus published market conduct examination reports and consent orders naming claims-handling findings at peer carriers.
For every item record the state, effective date, what changed (day count, notice content, documentation requirement) and whether the 30-day matrix-amendment clock was met.
Hand the Compliance Analyst a change list keyed to matrix rows and open an exception in the GRC platform for any change that sat past 30 days.
checklist.done: a dated change list mapped to matrix rows exists and every late amendment is logged as an exception.

checklist.step: Map every Model 900 standard to a numbered procedure section
actions: Build a two-column traceability table: left column Model 900 sections 4 through 10 as adopted, right column the CHS-900 section that implements each one.

Confirm every adopted prohibited practice has a named implementing section, including misrepresenting policy provisions, failing to act promptly on communications, compelling litigation by offering substantially less than amounts ultimately recovered, and failing to state a basis for denial.
Where the table shows a gap, raise a drafting task with an owner in the Claims organisation and a due date ahead of the counsel review.
Attach the traceability table to the draft as an appendix — examiners open it first.
checklist.done: every adopted Model 900 standard maps to a numbered CHS-900 section with no unassigned gaps.

checklist.step: Rewrite the acknowledgement standard with the per-state clocks
actions: State the trigger precisely: the acknowledgement clock starts at receipt of notification of claim by any channel — phone FNOL, portal, agent submission, email or mail.

Write the operating rule as the shortest applicable clock (Model 900 baseline of 15 working days, tightened to 10 days where a state requires it) and point to the matrix row for the state-specific count.
Specify the required content of the acknowledgement: claim number, adjuster name and direct contact, what the insured must supply next, and the DOI contact block where the state mandates it.
Specify what counts as proof of acknowledgement in the file: the system-generated letter with its send timestamp, not an adjuster note claiming a call was made.
Hand the drafted section to the Compliance Analyst to cross-check against every matrix row.
checklist.done: the acknowledgement section states trigger, per-state clock, required content and the evidence that proves it.

checklist.step: Rewrite the prompt-investigation and status-update standard
actions: Define the investigation start obligation: assignment to a named adjuster and first substantive contact attempt with the claimant, with the target working-day count from FNOL.
Write the 45-day rule: where a claim remains undecided, a written status letter goes to the claimant every 45 days stating the reason the decision is pending and what is still outstanding.
Prohibit the standing pattern examiners look for — repeated identical status letters with no changed reason — by requiring the letter to name the specific outstanding item and who owns it.
Set the documentation rule for delays outside the company's control (awaiting police report, medical records, engineer report) including the date requested and the follow-up cadence.
Reference the ClaimCenter diary activity that enforces the 45-day cycle so the written rule and the system rule are the same rule.
checklist.done: the section fixes the investigation start, the 45-day status cycle, its required content and the diary that enforces it.

checklist.step: Rewrite the coverage decision and accept/deny standard
actions: State the accept/deny clock measured from receipt of a completed proof of loss (Model 900 baseline 15 working days), pointing to the matrix for shorter state counts.
Define what constitutes a completed proof of loss for each line so the clock cannot be reset by asking for documents the company already holds.
Require the coverage analysis in the file to cite the policy form number, edition date and the specific provision relied on before any denial can be issued.
Require a supervisor review at defined authority thresholds and for every denial of a claim over the large-loss threshold, with the reviewer named in the file.
Prohibit closing a claim as no-payment without a written communication to the claimant stating the basis.
checklist.done: the section defines the proof-of-loss trigger, the decision clock, the citation requirement and the supervisory review points.

checklist.step: Rewrite the settlement, payment and good-faith evaluation standard
actions: Set the payment clock: funds issued within 5 business days of the settlement agreement or the execution of a release, unless the state matrix is shorter.

Require the evaluation to be supported in the file by the named source used — estimating platform valuation, medical bill review output, comparable-vehicle valuation report with its comparables listed, or reserve rationale — so an offer is never a bare number.

Ban the practices Model 900 names: offering substantially less than the amount ultimately recovered, conditioning payment on release of unrelated claims, and attempting to settle on an altered application.
Define the auto total-loss standard: valuation method, applicable taxes and title fees, and the itemised valuation report that must accompany the offer.
Set the escalation rule for any claimant dispute of an offer — routed to the supervisor within 2 business days with a documented re-evaluation.
checklist.done: payment clocks, evaluation support requirements, banned practices and the offer-dispute escalation are all written into the section.

checklist.step: Rewrite the denial-letter content standard
actions: Fix the mandatory content: the specific policy provision, exclusion or condition relied on quoted verbatim with form number and edition, the facts found, and the reason those facts trigger that provision.
Add the state-specific elements from the matrix: DOI name, address and telephone block, appeal or reconsideration rights, and any statutory notice language that must appear word for word.
Prohibit boilerplate denial reasons and require that any partial denial itemise what is paid and what is not.
Set the letter-template governance rule: templates are held in ClaimCenter, change only through Regulatory Counsel approval, and carry a template id and version stamped into each issued letter.
Approve the master denial template set and the per-state variants in writing.
checklist.done: the denial standard names every required element, its state variants, and locks templates behind counsel approval.

checklist.step: Rewrite the claim-file documentation standard
actions: Implement the Model 900 Section 4 rule: the file must contain all notes and work papers in enough detail that the events and dates can be reconstructed by a third party.
List the mandatory artifacts by claim type — FNOL record, acknowledgement letter, coverage analysis, estimates and valuations, status letters, settlement or denial letter, payment record, release.
Set naming and indexing rules in the claim file repository so an examiner request by claim number, state and closure date returns the complete file.
State the retention period as the longer of the state requirement and 7 years from claim closure, with legal hold overriding deletion.
Define the reconstruction test: a reviewer who never touched the claim must be able to build the date timeline from the file alone.
checklist.done: mandatory file artifacts, indexing, retention and the third-party reconstruction test are all specified.

checklist.step: Push the written standard into the ClaimCenter configuration
actions: For each jurisdiction set the acknowledgement, status-letter and accept/deny SLA values in the ClaimCenter business rules to the approved matrix values, using the loss-state on the claim as the driver rather than the insured's mailing state.
Configure the diary and escalation activities so an approaching acknowledgement or 45-day status deadline raises to the adjuster at T-3 days and to the supervisor at T-1.
Load the counsel-approved letter templates with their template ids and retire superseded versions so they cannot be selected.
Run the configuration in the test environment against a scripted set of claims per state and confirm the computed due dates match the matrix.
Export the configuration table (state, clock type, days, basis, template id) and attach it to the review folder as the reconciliation artifact.
checklist.done: ClaimCenter clocks and templates match the approved matrix and an exported configuration table proves it.

checklist.step: Route the draft through legal review
actions: Read the draft against the quoted state text captures rather than against the previous version, so an inherited error cannot survive another year.
Confirm each stricter-than-model state rule is stated as the operating rule and not buried in a footnote.
Write a review memo naming the sections reviewed, the changes required and the residual interpretation risks, and sign and date it.
Return required changes to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager with a due date ahead of the March 31 approval.
checklist.done: a signed, dated counsel review memo exists and every required change is either made or logged with a decision.

checklist.step: Obtain dual approval and set the effective date
actions: Present the redline, the counsel memo and the traceability table to the Chief Claims Officer for operational sign-off and sign the regulatory sufficiency approval yourself.
Record both signatures with dates on the approval page and set the manual's effective date at least 15 days after publication so training can land first.
Close the GRC review control record with the approval date, attaching the approved PDF, and confirm the March 31 due date was met.
Where March 31 was missed, open a procedure-currency exception with root cause and a remediation date rather than backdating the approval.
checklist.done: the manual carries two dated approval signatures, a stated effective date, and the GRC control is closed or an exception is open.

checklist.step: Publish, train and collect attestations
actions: Publish the approved manual to the claims intranet and retire the superseded version so only one version is reachable.

Build the change-focused training module covering the day counts that moved, the new denial-letter content and the file documentation rule, and assign it in the learning management system to every adjuster, examiner and claims supervisor within 15 days of publication.
Set the completion due date at the manual's effective date and require an attestation that the assignee has read the standards for the states they handle.
Chase non-completers weekly through their claims manager and report open completions to the Chief Claims Officer at the effective date.
checklist.done: training is assigned within 15 days, completion is tracked to the effective date, and open completions are reported by name.

checklist.step: File the evidence pack and apply retention
actions: Assemble the pack: approved manual and matrix, redline against baseline, dated state-text captures, counsel memo, ClaimCenter configuration export, approval page and LMS completion extract.
File it in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Claims Practices / <year> and apply the 7-year-from-supersession retention label.
Confirm the repository index makes the pack searchable by jurisdiction, manual version and approval date so an exam call letter can be answered in 5 business days.
Update the regulatory obligation register entry for the state adoptions of Model 900 with the new version and effective date.
checklist.done: the complete evidence pack is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by jurisdiction and version.

testing.step: Build the population of procedure sections and jurisdiction rows
actions: Extract from the compliance evidence repository every CHS-900 version effective at any point in the test year and the full 50-row Unfair Claims Requirement Matrix for each version.
Add the ClaimCenter configuration export and the letter-template inventory so system records join the population.
Reconcile the jurisdiction list to the licensing register of states where the company writes and resolve any state present in one and absent from the other before sampling.
testing.done: the population covers every in-force version and all 50 rows, reconciled to the licensing register and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the matrix to primary state text
actions: For each populated row confirm a dated state-text capture exists and that its capture date falls inside the review year.
Confirm the quoted sentence in the row actually appears in the capture and carries the section cite recorded.
List rows with no capture, a stale capture or a paraphrase in place of a quote as exceptions before any sampling judgement is made.
testing.done: every matrix row is either supported by an in-year dated capture with a matching quote or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of the jurisdictions flagged stricter-than-model and 100% of rows amended during the year following a bulletin.
Add 15 further states selected at random from a documented seed so the draw can be reproduced.
Record population size, seed, selection date and the resulting state list in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and includes every stricter-than-model and bulletin-amended jurisdiction.

testing.step: Re-derive the day counts independently from source text
actions: For each sampled state read the unfair claims act and regulation directly and write your own acknowledgement, status-interval, accept/deny and payment day counts before opening the matrix row.
Compare your derivation to the recorded row, treating a calendar-versus-working-day basis error as a full exception rather than a formatting note.
Confirm the manual states the shorter of the state count and the Model 900 baseline as the operating rule.
Capture the source page you relied on into the workpaper next to the re-performance note.
testing.done: each sampled state has an independent day-count derivation, a comparison result and a captured source page.

testing.step: Test the ClaimCenter configuration against the approved matrix
actions: Open the ClaimCenter business-rule configuration for the sampled states and compare the SLA day values and the calendar/working-day basis to the approved matrix row.
Create or inspect a test claim per sampled state and confirm the system-computed acknowledgement and accept/deny due dates equal the hand-computed dates.
Confirm the clock is driven by loss state and that retired letter templates cannot be selected.
Log any clock or template mismatch as a fail, since the written standard is inoperative wherever the system disagrees with it.
testing.done: system-computed due dates and template availability match the approved matrix for every sampled state, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Trace approval, version control and traceability evidence
actions: Confirm the in-force manual carries dated signatures from both the Chief Claims Officer and the Head of Compliance and that the signature dates precede the effective date.
Confirm the counsel review memo is signed, dated and references the version actually approved.
Open the Model 900 traceability table and confirm every adopted section maps to a numbered CHS-900 section with no blank right-hand cells.
Confirm only one version of the manual is reachable on the claims intranet.
testing.done: dual dated approvals, a matching counsel memo and a complete traceability table are evidenced, with a single live version.

testing.step: Test training assignment and attestation completeness
actions: Pull the LMS assignment and completion extract for the CHS-900 module and reconcile the assignee list to the HR roster of adjusters, examiners and claims supervisors as at the effective date.
Confirm assignment occurred within 15 days of publication and that completion was tracked to the effective date.
Sample 20 completions and confirm an attestation record exists naming the states the assignee handles.
List unassigned in-scope staff and open completions past the effective date as exceptions with the responsible claims manager named.
testing.done: the assigned population reconciles to the claims roster and every open or missing completion is named to a manager.

testing.step: Recompute the review-timeliness and bulletin-amendment maths
actions: Compare the approval date to the March 31 deadline and record the day variance.
For each bulletin in the year's regulatory-change list compute days from bulletin effective date to matrix amendment approval and test it against the 30-day clock.
Compute days from amendment approval to ClaimCenter configuration change and test it against the 45-day clock.
Present the three computations as a schedule with each breach shown in days rather than as a pass/fail flag.
testing.done: annual, 30-day and 45-day timeliness are each recomputed and every breach is quantified in days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception carrying the jurisdiction or section, what was wrong, and the exposure it creates in a market conduct exam.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — state text not refreshed, bulletin missed, matrix-to-system handoff failed, approval late, training not assigned — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any wrong day count that was live in production, commission a claim-level impact review of claims handled under it.
Carry every open issue into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate over sampled jurisdictions and compare it to the zero-tolerance day-count threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who drafted no sampled row, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and any live wrong day count to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement filing for every state/line combination that breaches the participation threshold; Market Conduct Compliance owns the narrative interrogatories and the officer attestation routing

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — MCAS is the data-collection arm of the states' Model 900 adoptions; the current year's NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions document for each participating line is re-read before extraction, alongside each participating state's MCAS bulletin or call notice (representative: Alabama Department of Insurance MCAS participation notice under the Alabama adoption of NAIC Model 900)

In-scope processes.value: MCAS scoping by state and line against the direct written premium threshold, source-system extraction of claim and policy counts, computation of the claim timeliness and disposition data elements per the Data Call definitions, edit-check clearance, interrogatory drafting, officer attestation and submission through the NAIC MCAS application

In-scope systems.value: Submission runs through the NAIC MCAS application reached from the NAIC state-based systems portal under the company's NAIC company code; the underlying claim counts come from Guidewire ClaimCenter and the premium and policy counts from the policy administration and statutory reporting stack

Compliance procedure documented.value: MCAS Filing Procedure — participation scoping test, element-by-element source-to-definition mapping workbook, extraction SQL under version control, reconciliation to Annual Statement Schedule T direct written premium, edit-check disposition log, interrogatory drafting and officer attestation routing

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager before each filing season opens, and re-approved whenever the NAIC changes the Data Call and Definitions for a participating line

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Data year is the prior calendar year; the NAIC MCAS submission window opens in February and the filing is due April 30 for property/casualty, life, annuity, long-term care, disability income and lender-placed lines, and June 30 for the health lines; internal cutoffs are extraction complete by March 1, edit checks cleared by March 31 and officer attestation signed by April 15

Deadline reminders configured.value: Regulatory reporting calendar entries fire at T-90 (scoping test), T-60 (extraction), T-30 (edit-check clearance) and T-15 (attestation) against April 30, with a parallel June 30 track for health lines and a daily countdown to the reporting manager in the final 10 days

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Submission confirmation number and receipt page per state and line, the final submitted data file, the extraction script version, the Schedule T reconciliation, the edit-check disposition log and the signed officer attestation are retained 7 years from the filing date in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any state/line filed after the deadline, any submission made with an unexplained edit-check warning, any post-submission resubmission and any state where the threshold was breached but no filing was made is logged with root cause and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late or amended MCAS submission and any self-report of a missed state/line to the relevant DOI

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every state/line combination where direct written premium for the data year met the MCAS participation threshold, joined to the submitted MCAS filings and their confirmation receipts, plus the underlying claim-level extract that produced the reported counts

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero missed state/line filings and zero filings after April 30 (June 30 for health) is the pass condition; reported claim counts must reconcile to the claim-level extract exactly, and reported premium must tie to Annual Statement Schedule T within 0.5% with any variance explained in writing

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs once per filing season immediately after submission closes and before the state follow-up window ends, so a resubmission can still be made inside the season

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Auditor must not have built the extract, cleared an edit check or drafted an interrogatory response for any sampled state/line

Evidence location for test results.value: MCAS filing test workpaper — scoping reconciliation, submission receipt inventory, recomputed count schedules and exception list — filed in the compliance evidence repository under Regulatory Reporting / MCAS / <data year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per state and line: the submitted data file, the confirmation receipt with its confirmation number and timestamp, the signed attestation and the Schedule T reconciliation, producible on a DOI data-integrity query within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting answers DOI data queries and files resubmissions through the NAIC MCAS application; Market Conduct Compliance owns any state follow-up that moves from data accuracy into claims-practice questions, with Regulatory Counsel clearing the response

checklist.step: Run the participation scoping test by state and line
actions: Extract direct written premium for the data year by state, by MCAS line and by writing company NAIC code from the statutory reporting stack, using the same basis as Annual Statement Schedule T.
Apply the MCAS participation threshold to each state/line/company cell and mark it IN SCOPE, OUT OF SCOPE or ZERO-PREMIUM.
Check each participating state's MCAS call notice or bulletin for a state-specific threshold or an added line before accepting the default test result.
Produce the scoping matrix showing state, line, company, NAIC code, DWP and the in-scope decision, and have the Regulatory Reporting Manager sign it.
Hand the signed matrix to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager as the definitive filing obligation list for the season.
checklist.done: a signed scoping matrix names every state/line/company that must file, with the DWP figure behind each decision.

checklist.step: Read the current-year Data Call and Definitions for each participating line
actions: Download the current NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions PDF for each line the company files and save it dated into the season folder.
Redline it against the prior year and list every changed data element, changed definition and new interrogatory.
For each change decide whether the extraction logic must move and raise a mapping change task with the Data Engineer.
Circulate the change list to Claims Operations so anyone whose counts will shift knows before the numbers appear.
checklist.done: a dated definitions document and a year-on-year change list exist for every filed line, with mapping tasks raised.

checklist.step: Refresh the element-to-source mapping workbook
actions: For every MCAS data element record the source system, table, field and the filter that implements the definition — for example claims closed with payment counted on closure date within the data year, by loss state.

Nail the definitions examiners test hardest: claims open at period start, opened during period, closed with and without payment, days-to-close buckets, suits opened and closed, and claims closed without payment beyond the state's decision clock.
Record for each element whether the count is by claim, by claimant or by feature, since misreading that is the most common MCAS restatement cause.
Have the Regulatory Reporting Manager review and sign the workbook before extraction begins.
checklist.done: every reported element has a signed source-field-filter mapping and a stated counting unit.

checklist.step: Extract the claim data for the data year
actions: Run the version-controlled extraction against the ClaimCenter reporting replica for loss dates and transaction dates spanning the data year, partitioned by loss state, line and writing company.
Output the claim-level detail file that supports every reported aggregate, keyed by claim number, so any reported cell can be drilled to the claims behind it.
Record the script commit hash, the run timestamp and the row counts in the extraction log.
Rerun after any late claim data correction and supersede the prior extract rather than patching it by hand.
checklist.done: a claim-level extract with a recorded commit hash and row counts supports every aggregate to be reported.

checklist.step: Compute the timeliness and disposition counts
actions: Aggregate the claim-level extract into the MCAS reporting cells per state, line and company using the signed mapping.
Compute the days-to-close and days-to-payment distributions into the exact buckets the Data Call defines, taking care that boundary days fall on the side the definition states.
Compute the claims-closed-without-payment counts and the counts closed beyond the state decision clock, since these drive the ratios states screen on.
Compare every cell to the prior data year and write a movement explanation for any cell moving more than 20%, sourced from Claims Operations rather than assumed.
checklist.done: all reporting cells are computed to the Data Call buckets with a written explanation behind every material year-on-year movement.

checklist.step: Reconcile premium and policy counts to the statutory filing
actions: Tie the MCAS direct written premium by state and line to Annual Statement Schedule T and the state page for the same data year.
Explain every difference in writing — line-grouping differences between MCAS lines and statutory lines are legitimate, unexplained differences are not.
Tie policy in-force and policy count elements to the policy administration extract used for statutory reporting.
Sign the reconciliation schedule and file it with the season folder as the artifact a DOI data query will ask for first.
checklist.done: MCAS premium and policy counts tie to Schedule T within 0.5% with every difference explained and the schedule signed.

checklist.step: Reconcile reported complaint counts to the consumer complaint record
actions: Extract from the complaint case management tool all DOI-received complaints for the data year by state and line, using date received by the company.
Reconcile the count to the NAIC complaint database records the company has been notified of, and investigate any complaint the DOI logged that never reached the internal register.
Split complaints by reason code so the claims-handling subset reported in MCAS is isolated from underwriting and marketing complaints.
Sign the complaint reconciliation and hand it to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst.
checklist.done: reported complaint counts reconcile to the internal register and to DOI-notified complaints, split by reason code.

checklist.step: Load the data and clear every edit check
actions: Log in to the NAIC MCAS application through the state-based systems portal under the company's NAIC company code and open the data year and line.
Upload the formatted submission file for each state and run the built-in validations.
Work every hard error to zero and give every soft warning a written explanation in the comment field rather than dismissing it silently.
Record each validation message, its disposition and the person who cleared it in the edit-check disposition log.
Never override a validation by changing a reported number without a corresponding change in the underlying extract.
checklist.done: all hard errors are cleared, every soft warning carries a written explanation, and the disposition log names who cleared what.

checklist.step: Draft the interrogatory responses
actions: Answer each interrogatory in the Data Call from documented fact — claim-handling systems used, use of third-party administrators, litigation and arbitration practices, and any material change in claim operations during the data year.
Where the answer describes a practice, cite the CHS-900 section that governs it so the narrative and the procedures cannot diverge.
Have Regulatory Counsel review any answer touching litigation practice or a known regulatory matter before it is entered.
Paste the approved text into the interrogatory fields and keep the approved source document in the season folder.
checklist.done: every interrogatory is answered from a counsel-reviewed source document cross-referenced to the procedures manual.

checklist.step: Route the officer attestation
actions: Review the summary pack: scoping matrix, reporting cells with year-on-year movements, the Schedule T reconciliation and the edit-check disposition log.
Question every unexplained movement before signing, since the attestation is a personal statement about the accuracy of the data.
Sign the attestation in the MCAS application for each state and line by the April 15 internal cutoff.
Return anything unsupported to Regulatory Reporting rather than attesting subject to caveat.
checklist.done: a signed officer attestation exists for every in-scope state and line, dated on or before April 15.

checklist.step: Submit each state and line and capture the receipt
actions: Submit each state/line filing in the NAIC MCAS application ahead of April 30 (June 30 for the health lines), starting with the largest states so a portal problem does not hit the deadline.
Capture the confirmation number, submission timestamp and submitted-by user for each filing and paste them into the submission tracker.
Screenshot the submitted status page per state and file it in the season folder.
Reconcile the tracker line by line to the signed scoping matrix and confirm no in-scope cell is unsubmitted.
checklist.done: every in-scope state/line shows a submitted status with a captured confirmation number, before its deadline.

checklist.step: Handle blank filings and threshold edge cases
actions: For any state/line where the company is registered as a participant but wrote no qualifying premium, file the zero or blank submission the state expects rather than simply not filing.
For companies that crossed the threshold for the first time this data year, confirm registration in the MCAS application before the window closes.
For companies that fell below the threshold, obtain the state's confirmation that no filing is required and file it as evidence.
Log each edge case with the state contact, date and the outcome.
checklist.done: every registered-but-non-writing and newly-crossing cell has either a submission or documented state confirmation that none is due.

checklist.step: Work state follow-up questions and any resubmission
actions: Monitor the MCAS application messages and the regulatory mailbox for state data-integrity queries after submission.
Trace each queried cell back through the claim-level extract to the underlying claims and answer with the drill-down attached.
Where an error is confirmed, prepare an amended submission, re-run the attestation and resubmit through the MCAS application, recording the amendment reason.
Open a tracker issue for any resubmission with root cause and a preventive action for next season.
checklist.done: every state query is answered from the claim-level extract and every confirmed error is resubmitted with a logged root cause.

checklist.step: Feed the reported ratios into conduct monitoring
actions: Load the submitted MCAS cells into the conduct monitoring dataset so the filed numbers and the quarterly internal metrics come from the same place.
Compare the company's timeliness and closed-without-payment ratios to the published MCAS benchmark ratios for each line and state.
Flag any state where the company sits in the tail of the distribution as an elevated market-analysis risk and brief the Chief Claims Officer.
Record the flagged states as inputs to the exam readiness file for the coming year.
checklist.done: filed MCAS ratios are benchmarked by state and every tail-of-distribution state is flagged and briefed.

checklist.step: Archive the season evidence pack
actions: Assemble per state and line: submitted data file, confirmation receipt, signed attestation, edit-check disposition log, Schedule T and complaint reconciliations, extraction commit hash and interrogatory source document.
File the pack in the compliance evidence repository under Regulatory Reporting / MCAS / <data year> and apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the index allows retrieval by state, line, confirmation number and data year.
Close the season control record in the regulatory reporting calendar with the actual submission dates recorded against the deadlines.
checklist.done: the full season pack is filed, retention-labelled, retrievable by confirmation number, and the season control is closed.

testing.step: Rebuild the population of required filings independently
actions: Pull direct written premium by state, line and company from the Annual Statement source rather than from the filing team's scoping matrix.
Apply the MCAS participation threshold and each state's call notice yourself to derive your own in-scope list.
Compare your list to the signed scoping matrix and treat any cell present in yours and absent from theirs as a potential missed filing to be resolved before sampling.
testing.done: an independently derived in-scope list exists and every difference from the scoping matrix is resolved.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to submission receipts
actions: Match every in-scope state/line to a confirmation number in the submission tracker and to a status page capture.
Compare each submission timestamp to April 30 (June 30 for health lines) and record the day variance, positive or negative.
List any in-scope cell with no confirmation number as an automatic fail and notify the Head of Compliance the same day rather than at report time.
testing.done: every in-scope cell traces to a confirmation number with a computed day variance to its deadline, or is escalated as a fail.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of reported cells
actions: Take 100% of the five largest states by direct written premium and 100% of cells that moved more than 20% year on year.
Add 10 further state/line cells drawn at random from a recorded seed.
Document population size, seed, draw date and the selected cell list in the workpaper so the draw can be reproduced.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers the largest states and every materially moved cell.

testing.step: Re-perform the reported counts from the claim-level extract
actions: For each sampled cell recompute the claim counts from the claim-level extract using the Data Call definition text, not the team's mapping workbook.
Recompute the days-to-close bucket allocation and check boundary days land on the side the definition states.
Check the counting unit actually used — claim, claimant or feature — matches the definition, and treat a unit mismatch as a restatement-level exception.
Record the reported figure, your figure and the difference for every sampled cell.
testing.done: every sampled cell carries an independent recomputation with the difference to the filed figure stated.

testing.step: Trace the extract back to individual claim files
actions: Select 25 claims from the sampled cells' claim-level detail and open each in ClaimCenter.
Confirm loss state, line, open and close dates, payment indicator and suit indicator on the claim match the values carried in the extract.

Confirm claims that should have been in the population — closed inside the data year in that state — were not dropped by a filter, by running a reverse check on 10 claims pulled directly from ClaimCenter.
Capture the ClaimCenter summary screen for each traced claim into the workpaper.
testing.done: traced claims agree with the extract in both directions and every trace has a captured source screen.

testing.step: Test the Schedule T and complaint reconciliations
actions: Re-add the reconciliation schedules and confirm the reported premium ties to Schedule T within the 0.5% tolerance for every sampled state.
Read each written variance explanation and confirm it names a real line-grouping or timing difference rather than restating the variance.
Recompute the claims-handling complaint count from the complaint case extract and compare it to the filed figure.
Confirm both reconciliations carry a signature and a date preceding submission.
testing.done: premium and complaint reconciliations are re-performed, within tolerance, explained and signed before submission.

testing.step: Test edit-check clearance and attestation integrity
actions: Read the edit-check disposition log and confirm every hard error shows a data fix traceable to an extract rerun, not a manual number change.
Confirm every soft warning carries a written explanation and the name of the person who cleared it.
Confirm the officer attestation for each sampled state is signed, dated on or before April 15, and postdates the final data load.
Flag any attestation signed before the last data change as a control failure.
testing.done: no cleared error lacks an extract-level fix and every attestation postdates the final data load.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline and cutoff maths
actions: Build a schedule of internal cutoffs actually met: extraction complete versus March 1, edit checks cleared versus March 31, attestation versus April 15, submission versus April 30 or June 30.
Compute the slack or overrun in days for each stage and each state, not just for the final submission.
Identify any state where submission succeeded only because a stage overran into someone else's buffer and call that out as a fragility even where no deadline was missed.
Present the schedule with the health-line June 30 track shown separately.
testing.done: every stage cutoff is recomputed in days by state, with buffer-consuming stages named even where the filing was on time.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the state, line, data element and the difference in units or days.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — scoping missed the cell, definition change not mapped, counting unit wrong, extract filter wrong, cutoff overrun — and an owner.
Where a filed figure is materially wrong, instruct an amended MCAS submission inside the season and record the amendment date.
Carry every open issue into next season's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where filed data was wrong, an amendment instruction.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate over sampled cells and compare it against the zero-missed-filing and exact-count thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who built no extract and cleared no edit check, sign as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion, any missed cell and any amendment to the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly Claims Conduct Scorecard and its benchmark thresholds; the Chief Claims Officer owns the operational response to any metric breaching a threshold

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the monitored metrics are drawn directly from the conduct standards in each state's adoption of NAIC Model 900 (acknowledgement, prompt investigation, accept/deny, prompt payment) and are benchmarked against published NAIC MCAS ratios and the state complaint index; the Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona adoptions of Model 900 are the representative texts behind the timeliness metrics

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly measurement of claims conduct across every open and closed claim in the quarter: acknowledgement timeliness, first-contact timeliness, 45-day status letter adherence, accept/deny timeliness from proof of loss, payment timeliness from settlement, closed-without-payment rate, reopened rate, litigation rate and DOI complaint volume, cut by state, line, claim office and adjuster

In-scope systems.value: The Claims Conduct Scorecard is published in Power BI over a governed dataset sourced from Guidewire ClaimCenter and the complaint case management tool; thresholds and breach dispositions are held with the scorecard definition document

Compliance procedure documented.value: Claims Conduct Monitoring Procedure — the metric definition dictionary (numerator, denominator, date basis, exclusions), the benchmark and threshold table by metric and state, the quarterly production and review calendar, the breach escalation path and the corrective-action intake

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Claims Officer; the metric definitions and thresholds are re-approved annually and whenever a state day count changes in the Unfair Claims Requirement Matrix, since the threshold is derived from the day count

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly cycle: data cut at quarter end, scorecard produced within 15 business days of quarter end, breach review meeting within 20 business days, corrective actions raised within 25 business days, and results into the Compliance Committee pack for the next scheduled sitting

Deadline reminders configured.value: Recurring calendar tasks fire on the first business day after quarter end (data cut), day 10 (draft scorecard), day 15 (publication) and day 20 (breach review) to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and the claims leadership distribution

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each quarter's published scorecard PDF, the underlying claim-level dataset snapshot, the threshold table version in force, the breach review minutes and the corrective actions raised are retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository, since examiners request trend evidence across multiple years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every metric breaching its threshold for a state or claim office is logged as a conduct-monitoring exception with the affected population size, root cause, owner and remediation date, and stays open until two consecutive quarters read inside threshold

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every threshold breach after two consecutive in-threshold quarters and approves any decision to accept a metric outside threshold

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All claims open or closed during the quarter across all lines and 50 jurisdictions as held in ClaimCenter, together with the published scorecard cells, the threshold table in force and the DOI complaint records for the same quarter

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Recomputed metric values must match the published scorecard within 0.5 percentage points per cell; any state cell where acknowledgement or accept/deny timeliness falls below 98% against the state's own day count is a breach requiring an open action; a breach carried three or more quarters without an owned action is an automatic fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly; the test runs quarterly over the quarter just published, with a full-year metric-definition review in Q1 so definition drift is caught annually

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Auditor must not build, own or publish the scorecard and must not report into the Claims organisation being measured

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly conduct-metric test workpaper — population reconciliation, recomputed metric schedule, sampled claim traces and the breach-ageing schedule — filed in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Monitoring / <year>-Q<n>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Four rolling quarters of published scorecards, the metric definition dictionary, the threshold table and the breach action log, producible for a market analysis inquiry or exam pre-work request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance responds to state market analysis inquiries and level-one analysis questions with the scorecard trend and the action log; Regulatory Counsel clears any response that concedes a pattern of practice

checklist.step: Confirm the metric dictionary still matches the state day counts
actions: Open the metric definition dictionary alongside the current Unfair Claims Requirement Matrix and confirm each timeliness metric measures against the state's own day count, not a single company-wide count.
Where a state day count changed in the quarter, update the metric threshold and record the effective quarter so trend charts show the break rather than hiding it.
Re-confirm each metric's numerator, denominator, date basis and exclusions in writing, especially claims closed and reopened inside the same quarter.
Publish the dictionary version that will govern this quarter's scorecard and freeze it before the data cut.
checklist.done: a frozen, versioned metric dictionary aligned to the current state day counts governs this quarter's production.

checklist.step: Take the quarter-end claim data cut
actions: On the first business day after quarter end run the governed extraction against the ClaimCenter reporting replica for all claims open at any point in the quarter, by loss state, line, claim office and adjuster.
Snapshot the extract so later claim edits cannot silently restate a published quarter, and record the snapshot id and row count.

Pull the paired events each metric needs: FNOL receipt timestamp, acknowledgement letter send timestamp, first contact attempt, each status letter send date, proof-of-loss receipt date, coverage decision date, settlement agreement date and payment issue date.
Hand the snapshot to the Report Developer with the dictionary version stamped on it.
checklist.done: an immutable quarter snapshot with all paired event timestamps and a recorded row count is handed over.

checklist.step: Compute the timeliness metrics against per-state clocks
actions: Compute acknowledgement timeliness as the share of claims acknowledged within the loss state's own day count, honouring calendar versus working-day basis per state.
Compute accept/deny timeliness from proof-of-loss receipt to coverage decision, and payment timeliness from settlement agreement to payment issue, each against the state count.
Compute 45-day status adherence as the share of undecided claim-months with a status letter sent inside the interval.
Publish each metric with its denominator visible on the tile so a small-population state cannot read as a crisis or a success on three claims.
Reconcile the sum of state denominators back to the snapshot row count before the numbers go anywhere.
checklist.done: timeliness metrics are computed against each state's own clock, show their denominators, and reconcile to the snapshot.

checklist.step: Compute the disposition and outcome metrics
actions: Compute the closed-without-payment rate by state and line, since it is the ratio state market analysts screen hardest on for Model 900 risk.
Compute the reopened-claim rate within 90 days of closure and the average days from FNOL to closure.
Compute the litigation rate as suits opened over claims closed, and the average time from suit to resolution.
Add a cut by adjuster and claim office so a company-level pass cannot conceal a single office driving the exposure.
checklist.done: disposition, reopen, cycle-time and litigation metrics are published with state, line, office and adjuster cuts.

checklist.step: Load DOI complaint data and compute the complaint index
actions: Extract from the complaint case management tool every DOI-originated complaint received in the quarter, by state, line and reason code.
Isolate the claims-handling reason codes — delay, denial, unsatisfactory settlement offer — that map to Model 900 conduct.
Compute complaints per 100,000 in-force policies by state and line and compare it to the published market average for the line.
List by name every complaint where the DOI response deadline was missed and hand it to the Complaints Manager the same day.
checklist.done: a state-level claims-handling complaint index is computed against market average and every missed DOI deadline is named.

checklist.step: Benchmark the metrics against MCAS ratios and peer distributions
actions: Line up each quarterly metric against the equivalent MCAS ratio the company most recently filed for that state and line, and against the published MCAS benchmark distribution.
Mark each state cell with its position — inside band, upper quartile of risk, or tail — using the threshold table rather than judgement.
Flag any state where the company sits in the risk tail on two or more metrics simultaneously, since that combination is what drives a state to open a market analysis review.
Write the benchmark commentary for the scorecard naming the states flagged and why.
checklist.done: every state cell carries a benchmark position and multi-metric tail states are flagged with written commentary.

checklist.step: Validate the data before publication
actions: Run completeness checks on the paired event timestamps and quantify claims with a missing acknowledgement or decision date rather than dropping them from the denominator.
Check for state assignment errors by comparing loss state to the policy state and investigating outliers, since a misassigned state moves the claim under the wrong clock.
Compare each metric to the prior quarter and require a written explanation from Claims Operations for any movement over 5 percentage points.
Sign the data quality certificate and attach it to the scorecard pack.
checklist.done: completeness, state-assignment and movement checks are run, explained and certified before publication.

checklist.step: Publish the quarterly Claims Conduct Scorecard
actions: Publish the scorecard within 15 business days of quarter end to the claims leadership and compliance distribution, with the dictionary version and snapshot id printed on the cover.
Show four rolling quarters per metric so trend, not a single quarter, drives the discussion.
Colour each state cell against the threshold table, with breaches listed on a single exceptions page rather than scattered through the deck.
Export the scorecard to PDF and file it in the compliance evidence repository as the immutable published version.
checklist.done: the scorecard is published inside 15 business days with rolling trend, a single exceptions page and an archived PDF.

checklist.step: Hold the quarterly breach review with claims leadership
actions: Convene the breach review within 20 business days of quarter end with the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and the responsible claim office leaders.
Take each breached state cell in turn and require the office to state the driver from claim evidence — staffing, intake backlog, a system routing defect, a single adjuster's caseload.
Decide for each breach: corrective action, accepted with rationale, or further analysis with a named date, and record which was chosen.
Minute the meeting with attendees, decisions and owners and file the minutes with the quarter's pack.
checklist.done: every breached cell has a minuted decision, a named driver and an owner within 20 business days of quarter end.

checklist.step: Raise and track corrective actions
actions: Open a GRC action per breach within 25 business days of quarter end carrying the state, metric, measured value, threshold and affected claim count.
Assign the accountable claim leader and a remediation date, and require the action to state the mechanism — reallocation, diary rule change, template fix, targeted coaching.
Set the closure rule explicitly: the action stays open until the metric reads inside threshold for two consecutive quarters.
Report ageing actions to the Head of Compliance monthly, with anything past three quarters escalated by name.
checklist.done: every breach has a GRC action with a mechanism, an owner, a date and a two-quarter closure rule.

checklist.step: Drive targeted claim file reviews where a metric breaches
actions: For each breached state cell pull 25 claims from the breaching population in ClaimCenter and review the file against the CHS-900 standard, not against the metric.
Record for each file whether the miss was real (letter never sent) or a data artifact (letter sent outside the system, timestamp missing), since the fix differs entirely.
Where the miss is real, check whether the claimant suffered detriment and refer any potential Model 900 breach to Regulatory Counsel.
Feed the review findings back into the breach action as the evidenced root cause.
checklist.done: each breached cell has a 25-file review distinguishing real misses from data artifacts, with detriment referred to counsel.

checklist.step: Route detriment cases into remediation
actions: Review every referred file where a Model 900 timeliness or good-faith standard was missed and the claimant was affected.
Determine whether interest, reimbursement or claim re-evaluation is owed under the state's statute and instruct Claims accordingly.
Decide, and record, whether any pattern requires proactive notification to the DOI rather than waiting for an exam to find it.
Sign the disposition on each referred file so the record shows a legal decision rather than an operational one.
checklist.done: every referred detriment file carries a signed counsel disposition and, where owed, an instruction to remediate the claimant.

checklist.step: Report to the Compliance Committee
actions: Present the quarter's scorecard summary, breached cells, action ageing and any counsel-referred detriment cases at the next scheduled Compliance Committee.
Name the states sitting in the risk tail on multiple metrics as elevated exam-likelihood jurisdictions.
Obtain committee direction on any metric being accepted outside threshold and minute it.
File the committee pack and minutes with the quarter's evidence.
checklist.done: the committee has seen the breaches, the ageing and the tail states, and any accepted breach is minuted.

checklist.step: Re-baseline thresholds where the underlying rule moved
actions: Compare the threshold table to the Unfair Claims Requirement Matrix and update any threshold whose state day count changed during the quarter.
Record the effective quarter of each threshold change alongside the metric so historical comparisons are not made against a moved goalpost.
Reissue the threshold table under a new version and have the Head of Compliance approve it.
Notify claims leadership of any state where the bar just moved, before the next quarter's data cut.
checklist.done: the threshold table is versioned, approved and aligned to the current state day counts, with changes dated and notified.

checklist.step: Archive the quarter's monitoring evidence
actions: File the published scorecard PDF, the snapshot dataset reference, the metric dictionary and threshold table versions, the data quality certificate, breach review minutes and the GRC action list under Market Conduct / Monitoring / <year>-Q<n>.
Apply the 7-year retention label so a multi-year trend request from an examiner can be met from the archive.
Confirm retrieval works by state, metric and quarter.
Update the exam readiness index with a pointer to the quarter's pack.
checklist.done: the quarter's monitoring pack is filed, retention-labelled, retrievable by state and metric, and indexed for exam readiness.

testing.step: Rebuild the quarter population from the source system
actions: Extract from ClaimCenter every claim open at any point in the quarter by loss state, line and claim office, independently of the published snapshot.
Reconcile your row count and state distribution to the snapshot row count recorded on the scorecard cover.
Investigate and resolve any difference — a claim absent from the snapshot is a monitoring blind spot, not a rounding issue — before sampling.
testing.done: an independently extracted population reconciles to the published snapshot with every difference resolved.

testing.step: Reconcile the published cells to the underlying dataset
actions: For every state cell on the scorecard confirm the displayed denominator equals the count of qualifying claims in the dataset.
Confirm the sum of state denominators equals the population, so no claim is measured twice or dropped by a filter.
List any cell whose denominator cannot be reproduced as an exception before any judgement on the metric value itself.
testing.done: every published denominator is reproduced from the dataset and the state denominators sum to the population.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of state cells and claims
actions: Take 100% of breached state cells and 100% of states flagged in the benchmark risk tail.
Add 10 further state cells at random from a recorded seed, and within each sampled cell draw 15 claims at random from the same seed.
Record population sizes, seed, draw date and the selected cells and claim numbers in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every breached and tail-flagged state cell plus claims within them.

testing.step: Re-perform the timeliness computation against the state clock
actions: For each sampled cell recompute acknowledgement, accept/deny and payment timeliness from the raw event timestamps using the state day count from the Unfair Claims Requirement Matrix, not from the metric dictionary.
Check the calendar-versus-working-day basis applied per state and treat a basis error as a full exception, since it moves every claim in the state.
Compare your value to the published value and record the difference in percentage points against the 0.5 point tolerance.
Capture the computation workings in the workpaper so the recomputation itself can be re-performed.
testing.done: each sampled cell has an independent timeliness recomputation with the variance to the published figure stated.

testing.step: Trace sampled claims to the file evidence
actions: For each sampled claim open the file repository and locate the acknowledgement letter, status letters, coverage decision letter and payment record.
Confirm the document send dates match the timestamps the metric used, and that a letter counted as sent actually exists as a document.
Confirm any claim scored as compliant on a manually recorded date has supporting correspondence, since manual dates are where timeliness metrics inflate.
Capture the document list and dates per claim into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled claim's counted events are supported by a dated document in the file, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Test the complaint index and the DOI response record
actions: Recompute complaints per 100,000 in-force policies for the sampled states from the complaint case extract and the policy in-force count.
Confirm the claims-handling reason-code split matches the underlying case records rather than a stale mapping.
For 10 complaints check the DOI response was sent inside the state's response deadline and that the response is in the case record.
List any DOI complaint missing from the internal register as a reportable control failure.
testing.done: the complaint index is recomputed, the reason-code split verified, and every sampled DOI response deadline tested.

testing.step: Test the benchmark placement and threshold table version
actions: Confirm the threshold table version stamped on the scorecard matches the version approved by the Head of Compliance for that quarter.
Re-place each sampled state cell against the threshold and the MCAS benchmark distribution and compare to the published colour.
Confirm any threshold changed during the quarter is dated and that trend charts show the break rather than restating history.
Flag any cell coloured inside band that your placement puts in breach as a suppression exception.
testing.done: threshold versioning is verified and every sampled cell's benchmark placement is independently re-derived.

testing.step: Recompute breach ageing and action timeliness
actions: Extract all open conduct-monitoring actions and compute, per action, the number of consecutive quarters the underlying metric has been in breach.
Compute days from quarter end to scorecard publication, to breach review and to action creation, and test each against the 15, 20 and 25 business-day cutoffs.
Confirm no action was closed before two consecutive in-threshold quarters and reopen any that was.
Present breaches aged three or more quarters as a named schedule regardless of whether an action exists.
testing.done: breach ageing and the 15/20/25-day cutoffs are recomputed and every premature closure is identified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the state cell or claim, the metric, and the variance in points or days.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — wrong state clock applied, missing event timestamp, denominator filter wrong, threshold table stale, breach not actioned in time — and an owner.
Where the recomputation shows a real conduct miss that the scorecard concealed, refer the affected claim population to Regulatory Counsel for detriment assessment.
Carry every open exception into next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, with concealed conduct misses referred to counsel.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate over sampled cells and compare it to the 0.5 point recomputation tolerance and the 98% timeliness breach threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references behind each supporting point.
Have the Internal Auditor, who neither builds nor owns the scorecard, sign as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion, any suppressed breach and any counsel referral to the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the standing market conduct exam readiness file and acts as the single company liaison to the examiner-in-charge; the Chief Claims Officer owns availability of claims staff and files during an exam

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the readiness file is built to the claims standards in the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook as adopted by the examining state, sitting on top of that state's own unfair claims settlement practices act (representative: Alabama Ala. Admin. Code r. 482-1-125 with Arkansas and Arizona adoptions of NAIC Model 900), with each state's exam authority statute confirmed before an exam opens

In-scope processes.value: Continuous maintenance of the exam-ready evidence set: claim file completeness and retrievability, the standing claims data extract in examiner format, procedure and training records, prior exam and complaint history, third-party administrator and vendor oversight records, and the exam response workflow from call letter through to draft report

In-scope systems.value: Claim files and correspondence are produced from the claim file repository indexed by claim number, state and closure date; the standing data extract is generated from Guidewire ClaimCenter and the readiness index and exam correspondence are held in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Market Conduct Exam Readiness Procedure — the readiness index, the standing claims data extract specification in examiner-acceptable layout, the claim file assembly standard, the document request intake and privilege review workflow, the interview preparation protocol and the draft-report response process

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Chief Claims Officer; the readiness index is refreshed quarterly and the procedure re-approved annually or after every completed exam, whichever comes first, with the lessons from that exam written in

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous obligation with hard exam clocks once an exam opens: acknowledge the call letter within 5 business days, deliver the initial standardised data request inside the period the examiner sets (commonly 10 to 30 days), deliver sampled claim files within the examiner's per-request window, and respond to the draft report within the 30 days the Market Regulation Handbook process allows; internally the readiness index is refreshed within 20 business days of each quarter end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Quarterly readiness refresh tasks fire at quarter end plus 5 and plus 15 business days; once an exam opens, every examiner request is loaded into the exam tracker with its own due date and alerts at T-5 and T-2 business days to the request owner and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Readiness index versions, quarterly data extracts, the full exam correspondence file, every document produced to an examiner with its production date and request reference, the draft and final reports and the company response are retained 10 years from exam closure — longer than the claim retention, because the next examiner will ask about the last exam

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any claim file that cannot be produced complete within the examiner window, any missed request due date, and any readiness index item found stale at the quarterly refresh is logged with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every readiness gap and approves every production of documents to an examiner after the privilege review

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The readiness index items in force for the period, the quarterly standing data extracts, a population of closed claims across the 50 jurisdictions drawn as an examiner would draw it, and every examiner request logged in the exam tracker during the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of test-requested claim files must be produced complete within the simulated examiner window of 10 business days; any file missing a mandatory artifact from the CHS-900 documentation standard is a fail; any readiness index item stale beyond one quarter is a fail; any real examiner request delivered late is an automatic fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; readiness is tested quarterly by a mock request, and a full mock exam covering data extract, file production and interview readiness is run annually in a jurisdiction flagged as elevated exam-likelihood by the conduct scorecard

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Auditor runs the mock request as an examiner would and must not maintain the readiness index or assemble claim files

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly exam readiness test workpaper — mock request letter, production log with timestamps, file completeness scoring sheet and the gap schedule — filed in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Exam Readiness / <year>-Q<n>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The readiness pack itself: current claims procedures, organisation and authority chart, standing claims data extract, prior exam reports and their remediation status, complaint register, TPA oversight records and training completion, producible on a call letter within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager is the single point of contact to the examiner-in-charge; all productions route through Regulatory Counsel for privilege review, and no claims employee answers an examiner question outside a scheduled, prepared interview

checklist.step: Maintain the readiness index as a living inventory
actions: Hold in the compliance evidence repository a single readiness index listing every item an examiner routinely requests, its owner, its refresh cycle, its current version and the date last refreshed.

Populate it against the claims standards an examiner works to: written claims procedures, organisational and settlement authority chart, claim system description and data dictionary, complaint register, TPA and vendor list, training records, and prior exam reports with remediation status.
Mark every item red once it passes its refresh cycle and chase the owner rather than waiting for a call letter to discover it.
Review the index at quarter end plus 15 business days with the Chief Claims Officer's delegate and record the review date.
checklist.done: the index shows every routinely requested item with an owner, a version, a refresh date and no item past its cycle.
