checklist.step: Keep the standing claims data extract examiner-ready
actions: Maintain a versioned extract from ClaimCenter in the layout examiners ask for: one row per claim with claim number, policy number, loss state, line, loss date, report date, acknowledgement date, first contact date, coverage decision date and outcome, settlement date, payment amounts and dates, closure date, reopen flag, suit flag and denial reason code.
Refresh the extract quarterly for a rolling five-year window, since exam scope periods routinely reach back three to five years.
Produce it in a delimited flat file with a published record layout and data dictionary so the examiner's analytics tooling can load it without a negotiation.
Run row-count and null checks on the key date fields and record the results with the extract version.
Store each version with its generation date so the exact file given to an examiner can be reproduced later.
checklist.done: a documented, quality-checked five-year claims extract in examiner layout exists and refreshes quarterly.

checklist.step: Prove claim files are retrievable and complete
actions: Confirm the claim file repository indexes every claim by claim number, loss state, line, closure date and adjuster so an examiner sample can be pulled on any of those keys.
Run a quarterly retrievability sweep on 50 randomly selected closed claims and time how long a complete file assembly takes end to end.

Score each assembled file against the CHS-900 mandatory artifact list — FNOL record, acknowledgement, coverage analysis, estimates and valuations, status letters, decision letter, payment record, release.
Escalate any storage tier, archived system or acquired-book repository where files cannot be produced inside 10 business days.
Record the sweep results and assembly times in the readiness index.
checklist.done: a quarterly sweep evidences complete file assembly inside 10 business days, with problem repositories escalated by name.

checklist.step: Keep legacy and acquired-book claim data reachable
actions: List every decommissioned or acquired claim system holding claims inside the five-year exam window and where its data now sits.
For each, document the retrieval route, the responsible team and the tested time to produce a claim file, and test it on 5 claims per system each quarter.
Where retrieval depends on an individual or an unsupported application, raise a readiness gap with a remediation date rather than a workaround note.
Record the mapping in the readiness index so an examiner's sample landing on a legacy claim does not stall the exam.
checklist.done: every legacy and acquired claim source has a tested, documented retrieval route with a measured production time.

checklist.step: Maintain the procedures, authority and organisation pack
actions: Hold current copies of CHS-900 and the Unfair Claims Requirement Matrix, with version history and approval signatures, ready to produce.
Maintain the settlement authority matrix showing dollar authority by role and the escalation points, dated and approved.
Maintain the claims organisation chart with named leaders by line and region and the count of adjusters by state.
Refresh all three quarterly and stamp each with the refresh date so nothing dated two years back reaches an examiner.
checklist.done: procedures, settlement authority matrix and organisation chart are all current, dated and production-ready.

checklist.step: Maintain the complaint and litigation history
actions: Maintain a five-year DOI complaint register by state, line, reason code, receipt date, response date and outcome, reconciled to DOI notifications.
Maintain the extra-contractual and bad-faith litigation register with matter, state, allegation type, status and resolution, sourced from the legal matter system.
Reconcile both registers quarterly and investigate any DOI complaint or suit that never entered the register.
Hold the register export in the readiness pack so it is produced complete rather than assembled under exam pressure.
checklist.done: five-year complaint and bad-faith litigation registers are reconciled quarterly and held production-ready.

checklist.step: Maintain third-party administrator and vendor oversight records
actions: List every TPA, independent adjusting firm, estimating vendor and salvage or medical bill review vendor that touches claim handling, with the states and lines they serve.
For each hold the current contract, the TPA licence or registration in the states served, the oversight audit reports and the service standards tied to the Model 900 clocks.
Confirm the delegated authority granted to each vendor does not exceed what the settlement authority matrix permits.
Refresh the pack quarterly and escalate any vendor without a current oversight audit as a readiness gap.
checklist.done: every claims vendor has a current contract, state licence evidence, oversight audit and an authority check on file.

checklist.step: Maintain claims training and licensing evidence
actions: Extract quarterly from the learning management system the completion record for the CHS-900 unfair claims module by named adjuster and state handled.
Hold the adjuster licensing register for the states requiring adjuster licences, with licence numbers and expiry dates, and flag anything expiring within 90 days.
Confirm any adjuster handling claims in a licensing state holds the licence for that state before the exam finds the gap.
File both extracts in the readiness pack with their extract dates.
checklist.done: current training completion and adjuster licensing extracts are held with expiries inside 90 days already flagged.

checklist.step: Track prior exam findings and their remediation status
actions: Hold every prior market conduct exam report from the last 10 years with the finding list, the agreed corrective actions and the current closure status from the GRC platform.
For each closed finding hold the validation evidence, since a new examiner will test whether the last examiner's finding actually got fixed.
Flag any finding closed without validation evidence as an urgent readiness gap.
Summarise the position on one page — exam, state, year, findings, closed, open — as the first thing handed to a new examiner.
checklist.done: every prior finding shows a status with validation evidence and the one-page summary is current.

checklist.step: Run the call-letter response drill
actions: Define the first-72-hours protocol: acknowledge the call letter within 5 business days, confirm the examiner-in-charge, exam scope period, lines and states, and the coordination status if it is a multistate exam.
Name the exam response team in advance — compliance lead, claims operations lead, data lead, counsel — with named deputies.
Issue the document hold notice to Claims, IT and Records the day the call letter arrives and record its distribution.
Rehearse the protocol at least annually and record the drill date and the elapsed times achieved.
checklist.done: a named response team, a 5-business-day acknowledgement protocol and a rehearsed hold-notice process are documented.

checklist.step: Operate the examiner request tracker during an exam
actions: Log every examiner request the day it arrives with the request number, exact wording, examiner name, due date and assigned owner.
Break composite requests into deliverables so a single unmet element cannot make an entire response late.
Track production status daily and alert the owner at T-5 and T-2 business days.
Record the actual production date, the delivery channel and the document list for each request so the production history reconstructs itself.
checklist.done: every examiner request is logged with wording, owner, due date and an actual production record.

checklist.step: Run privilege and accuracy review before any production
actions: Review every document set before it leaves the company for privileged material, unrelated personal data and inaccurate statements.
Withhold privileged items with a logged basis rather than silently removing pages, and produce the log where the examiner's process expects one.
Confirm the produced set actually answers the request as worded, since an incomplete production generates a follow-up finding of its own.
Sign the production approval and record it against the request in the tracker.
checklist.done: no document reaches an examiner without a signed counsel review and a logged basis for anything withheld.

checklist.step: Prepare staff for examiner interviews
actions: Identify the adjusters, supervisors and system owners the examiner has asked to interview and confirm scheduling through the single point of contact.
Brief each interviewee on the exam scope, the procedure sections that govern their work, and the rule that they answer from knowledge and say so when they do not know.
Have compliance or counsel attend every interview and take a contemporaneous note filed against the exam record.
Feed any factual correction arising in an interview back to the examiner in writing the same week.
checklist.done: every interviewee is briefed, accompanied and noted, with factual corrections issued in writing within the week.

checklist.step: Reconcile examiner sample findings against the file before the draft report
actions: For every claim the examiner criticises, pull the full file and rebuild the date timeline from source records in ClaimCenter and the file repository.
Distinguish real breaches from evidence gaps where the action occurred but was recorded outside the system, and gather the supporting record for the latter.
Prepare a per-claim written response with the evidence attached and hand it to the examiner before the draft report closes, where the process allows.
Log every real breach immediately as a remediation item rather than waiting for the report to make it official.
checklist.done: every criticised claim has a rebuilt timeline and a written, evidenced response before the draft report closes.

checklist.step: Refresh the readiness pack after every exam and every quarter
actions: Within 20 business days of quarter end confirm every readiness index item was refreshed and sign the index version.
After each completed exam write the lessons into the readiness procedure — the requests that were hard to meet, the data fields the examiner needed, the files that took too long.
File the entire exam record (call letter, requests, productions, interview notes, draft and final report, company response) under 10-year retention in the compliance evidence repository.
Report readiness status and any open gap to the Compliance Committee each quarter.
checklist.done: the index is signed each quarter, exam lessons are written into the procedure and the full exam record is filed under 10-year retention.

testing.step: Build the readiness population and the mock exam scope
actions: Extract the readiness index in force for the quarter with every item, owner, refresh cycle and last-refresh date.
Select a mock exam scope as a state examiner would: one jurisdiction flagged elevated by the conduct scorecard, a three-year scope period, and the personal lines written there.
Build the claim population for that scope directly from ClaimCenter rather than from the standing extract, so the extract itself can be tested against it.
testing.done: the readiness index population and an independently built mock-scope claim population both exist.

testing.step: Reconcile the standing extract to the source system
actions: Compare the standing claims extract for the mock scope to your ClaimCenter population on claim count, state, line and closure date.
Confirm the extract covers the full five-year rolling window and that the record layout and data dictionary match the file actually produced.
Test the key date fields for nulls — acknowledgement, decision, payment, closure — and quantify the null rate, since an examiner will read nulls as non-compliance.
List any claim present in ClaimCenter and absent from the extract as an exception before proceeding.
testing.done: the standing extract reconciles to ClaimCenter on count and scope, with null rates quantified per key date field.

testing.step: Draw the mock examiner sample and document it
actions: Draw 50 closed claims from the mock scope using a seeded random selection, weighted to include closed-without-payment and denied claims as an examiner would.
Add 10 claims from legacy or acquired-book systems inside the scope period to test the hardest retrieval route.
Record population size, seed, weighting rationale, draw date and the claim numbers in the workpaper.
Issue the sample as a formal mock request letter with a 10-business-day due date, addressed as an examiner would address it.
testing.done: a reproducible, examiner-weighted sample is issued as a dated mock request with a 10-business-day clock.

testing.step: Time and score the file production
actions: Record the delivery timestamp of each produced file and compute elapsed business days against the 10-day window.
Score each file against the CHS-900 mandatory artifact list and mark any missing artifact as an incomplete production, not a minor gap.
Apply the reconstruction test: decide from the file alone whether the claim's date timeline can be rebuilt by someone who never touched it.
Record the per-file score, elapsed days and the reconstruction verdict in the scoring sheet.
testing.done: every requested file has an elapsed-days figure, an artifact completeness score and a reconstruction verdict.

testing.step: Re-perform the conduct assessment on the sampled files
actions: For each produced file compute acknowledgement, decision and payment elapsed days from the documents themselves and compare them to the state day counts in the Unfair Claims Requirement Matrix.
For denied claims confirm the letter quotes the policy provision with form number and edition and carries the state's required DOI contact block.
For claims closed without payment confirm a written communication to the claimant states the basis.
List each conduct miss the way an examiner would state it, citing the standard and the claim number.
testing.done: each sampled file carries an independent conduct assessment written as an examiner-style finding where it fails.

testing.step: Test the supporting readiness records
actions: Pull the settlement authority matrix, organisation chart, TPA and vendor pack, training extract and adjuster licensing register and check each against its refresh cycle date.
For the mock jurisdiction confirm every adjuster who touched a sampled claim held the state adjuster licence at the time and completed the CHS-900 module.
Confirm every vendor touching a sampled claim has a current contract, oversight audit and authority within the settlement matrix.
List any item past its refresh cycle by more than one quarter as a fail.
testing.done: every supporting readiness record is in cycle, and adjuster licensing and vendor oversight are verified for the sampled claims.

testing.step: Test the prior-finding remediation evidence
actions: Take every finding from the last two market conduct exams and confirm the GRC record shows a status and, for closed items, validation evidence.
Re-perform the validation for 5 closed findings by testing the control as it operates today rather than reading the closure memo.
Treat any finding closed without evidence, or whose control has since drifted, as a repeat-finding risk and name it as such.
Confirm the one-page prior-exam summary matches the GRC record.
testing.done: prior findings are status-verified, five closures are independently re-validated and repeat-finding risks are named.

testing.step: Recompute the exam-clock and refresh timeliness maths
actions: For every real examiner request logged in the period compute days from receipt to production against the examiner's due date and list every overrun in days.
Compute days from call letter to acknowledgement against the 5-business-day protocol and days from draft report to company response against the 30-day window.
Compute days from each quarter end to readiness index sign-off against the 20-business-day cutoff.
Present all three as a single timeliness schedule rather than as narrative.
testing.done: request, call-letter, draft-report and quarterly refresh clocks are each recomputed with overruns stated in days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the claim, index item or request, and what an examiner would have concluded from it.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — file artifact missing, legacy retrieval route broken, index item stale, extract field null, request owner missed the date — and an owner.
For every conduct miss found in the mock sample, refer the claim to Regulatory Counsel for detriment assessment rather than treating it as a documentation issue.
Carry every open issue into next quarter's readiness test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, with real conduct misses referred to counsel.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the production completeness rate and the on-time rate against the 100%-within-10-business-days threshold.
Write the conclusion — exam ready, ready with exceptions, or not ready — with the workpaper references behind it, and state plainly which jurisdictions the company could not currently satisfy.
Have the Internal Auditor, who maintains no readiness item and assembles no file, sign as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and any not-ready jurisdiction to the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper under 10-year retention in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states production rates, a readiness conclusion by jurisdiction and the committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the exam-finding remediation programme end to end; the Chief Claims Officer owns delivery of each operational corrective action and the Head of Compliance owns the commitment made back to the department of insurance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the remediation obligation flows from the examining state's exam authority statute and any regulatory settlement agreement or consent order, read together with the state's unfair claims settlement practices act that the finding was written against (representative: Alabama Ala. Admin. Code r. 482-1-125 under the Alabama adoption of NAIC Model 900; Arkansas and Arizona adoptions apply where those states examine)

In-scope processes.value: Event-driven remediation from receipt of a draft market conduct exam report: finding validation, corrective action plan design, claimant restitution or re-adjudication where detriment occurred, procedure and system change, targeted retraining, evidence-backed closure, regulator reporting and the follow-up examination response

In-scope systems.value: Every finding, corrective action, milestone and validation record is held in the GRC platform as the single source of remediation status; claim re-adjudication and restitution payments are executed in Guidewire ClaimCenter so the remediation is visible on the claim itself

Compliance procedure documented.value: Exam Finding Remediation Procedure — draft report review and factual challenge, finding acceptance, root cause analysis, corrective action plan with milestones and owners, affected-population identification and restitution calculation, validation testing standard, regulator status reporting and closure sign-off

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Claims Officer; the corrective action plan for each individual exam is additionally approved by the Compliance Committee before it is submitted to the department, and by Regulatory Counsel where it is a term of a settlement agreement

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Response to the draft report within the 30 days the exam process allows; corrective action plan to the department within the period the final report or settlement agreement specifies (commonly 30 to 60 days from the final report); restitution completed by the date in the agreement; interim status reports on the cadence the department sets (commonly quarterly); each internal milestone tracked to its own agreed date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Each finding in the GRC platform carries its regulator-agreed date with escalating alerts at T-30, T-14, T-7 and T-1 days to the action owner, the Compliance Manager and, inside 7 days, the Head of Compliance; the department status-report date is a separate hard-stop calendar entry

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Draft and final exam reports, the company response, the approved corrective action plan, all root cause analyses, restitution registers and payment proofs, validation test workpapers, department correspondence and the closure letter are retained 10 years from finding closure in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any milestone missed against a regulator-agreed date, any finding closed without validation evidence and any restitution payment not made by the agreed date is logged as a remediation exception, escalated to the Head of Compliance and disclosed in the next status report to the department

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs closure of every finding only against validation evidence, and personally signs every status report and closure representation made to the department

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every finding from every market conduct examination, regulatory settlement agreement or consent order open at any point in the period, with its corrective actions, milestones, validation records, restitution register and department correspondence

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero findings closed without validation evidence and zero missed regulator-agreed dates is the pass condition; restitution must be 100% complete against the identified affected population with payment proof per claimant; any repeat of a prior exam finding is an automatic ineffective conclusion regardless of the rest of the population

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven per exam; the test runs on every finding closure before the closure is asserted to the department, plus a quarterly sweep of all open findings so a slipping milestone is caught before the regulator's status-report date

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Independent validation is owned by Internal Audit reporting to the Chief Audit Executive, who signs closure validation and must not sit in the Compliance or Claims reporting line that delivered the action

Evidence location for test results.value: Per-finding closure validation workpaper — finding text, corrective action, population, re-performance results, restitution proof and the signed validation opinion — filed in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Exam Remediation / <state>-<exam year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: For each finding: the accepted finding text, root cause analysis, approved corrective action plan, milestone completion evidence, restitution register with payment proofs and the independent validation opinion, producible for a follow-up examination or a status-report challenge within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Head of Compliance signs and submits every response and status report to the examining department through the exam contact; Regulatory Counsel clears all correspondence, and any admission of a continuing violation or any offer of restitution beyond the finding is approved by counsel before it is sent

checklist.step: Review the draft report and challenge the facts before it is final
actions: On receipt of the draft market conduct report open a response file and diarise the 30-day response window from the date of receipt.
Take each criticism to the underlying claim file and rebuild the timeline from source records, separating factual errors from findings that are simply unwelcome.
Draft the response as a per-finding table: finding number, examiner statement, company position (accept / accept in part / factually contest), and the exhibit reference behind any challenge.
Have Regulatory Counsel review every contested finding and sign the response before submission.
Submit inside the 30-day window and record the submission date and channel.
checklist.done: a counsel-signed, exhibit-backed per-finding response is submitted inside the 30-day draft report window.

checklist.step: Register every accepted finding with a regulator-agreed date
actions: On receipt of the final report create one GRC record per finding carrying the verbatim finding text, the standard cited, the state, the exam year and the examiner's error rate or sample result.
Record the date the department requires the corrective action plan and the date any settlement agreement or consent order sets for completion.
Assign an accountable executive owner per finding — never a team — and a compliance lead.
Link each finding to the CHS-900 section and the conduct metric it touches so remediation and monitoring stay joined up.
Never merge two findings into one record; the department will close them separately.
checklist.done: every final-report finding has its own GRC record with verbatim text, regulator dates, an executive owner and a procedure link.

checklist.step: Run root cause analysis on each finding
actions: For each finding pull the examiner's sampled claims and a wider internal sample of the same population, and establish whether the cause was procedure, system configuration, capacity, training or supervision.
Test the obvious explanation before accepting it — a training conclusion for a finding actually caused by a ClaimCenter diary rule will produce a repeat finding.
Quantify how long the cause has been live and therefore how far back the affected population reaches.
Write the analysis as a one-page document per finding with the evidence attached, and have the accountable executive sign it.
checklist.done: each finding has a signed, evidenced root cause naming the mechanism and the period over which it operated.

checklist.step: Identify the full affected claim population
actions: Translate each root cause into a query over ClaimCenter that finds every claim exposed to it, not only the claims the examiner sampled.
Run the query across the whole period the cause was live and across every state where the same procedure or configuration applied, since a finding in one state usually implicates its neighbours.
Produce a claim-level affected population file with claim number, state, line, claimant, closure date and the specific defect present.
Have the Data Quality Analyst independently reconcile the population to the source and sign it before any restitution maths begins.
checklist.done: a signed, reconciled claim-level affected population exists covering every state and the full period the cause was live.

checklist.step: Compute restitution and re-adjudication owed
actions: For each affected claim determine the remedy: re-adjudicate the coverage decision, pay the shortfall, pay statutory interest for late payment, or issue the notice that was never sent.
Compute interest at the state's statutory rate from the date payment was due to the date it will be made, and show the calculation per claimant rather than as a block sum.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the remedy meets the state's requirement and the terms of any settlement agreement.
Build the restitution register: claimant, claim number, state, remedy type, amount, interest, due date and status.
checklist.done: the restitution register carries a per-claimant remedy, amount, interest calculation and due date, cleared by counsel.

checklist.step: Build the corrective action plan the department will hold you to
actions: Write one plan per finding: the corrective action, the mechanism (procedure change, system configuration, staffing, supervision, training), the milestone dates, the owner and the evidence that will prove completion.
Set milestone dates that are genuinely achievable and back them off the regulator-agreed completion date rather than forward from today.
State the validation method for each action up front — what Internal Audit will test and against what threshold — so closure cannot later be argued.
Include the restitution timetable and the reporting cadence the department set.
Do not commit in the plan to anything the operation has not agreed it can deliver.
checklist.done: each finding has a plan with mechanism, dated milestones, an owner, a stated validation method and an agreed evidence set.

checklist.step: Get the plan approved and submitted to the department
actions: Take the consolidated plan to the Compliance Committee for approval, presenting cost, delivery risk and the consequence of a missed regulator date.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the wording, particularly anything that could read as an admission beyond the accepted finding.
Sign and submit the plan to the examining department inside the window the final report or settlement agreement set, and record the submission date and the department contact.
Load the submitted dates into the GRC records as the authoritative deadlines, replacing any earlier internal estimate.
checklist.done: a committee-approved, counsel-cleared plan is submitted on time and its dates are the ones tracked in GRC.

checklist.step: Change the procedure that produced the finding
actions: Amend the affected CHS-900 section and Unfair Claims Requirement Matrix row inside the 30-day out-of-cycle amendment clock the procedure sets.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the amendment against the standard the finding cited, so the fix addresses the cited standard rather than the examiner's example.
Obtain the Chief Claims Officer and Head of Compliance approvals and set the effective date.
Attach the approved amendment to the finding's GRC record as milestone evidence.
checklist.done: the procedure is amended, counsel-reviewed, dually approved and attached to the finding record inside 30 days.

checklist.step: Change the system configuration and prove it in production
actions: Raise the ClaimCenter change for the defective SLA clock, diary rule, routing rule or letter template identified as the cause, referencing the finding number in the change record.
Test in the non-production environment against scripted claims for every affected state and confirm the computed dates and generated letters are now correct.
Deploy and then verify on live claims created after the release, capturing before-and-after screenshots into the finding record.
Retire the defective template or rule so it cannot be selected, rather than leaving it available alongside the corrected one.
checklist.done: the configuration change is deployed, verified on post-release live claims and evidenced with before-and-after captures.

checklist.step: Execute restitution and re-adjudication on the affected claims
actions: Reopen each affected claim in ClaimCenter under the exam remediation reason code so the population stays identifiable for the follow-up exam.
Re-adjudicate or issue the additional payment and interest per the restitution register, and issue the claimant letter explaining what was found and what is being paid.
Where a claimant cannot be located, follow the state's unclaimed property route and document each locate attempt with its date.
Update the restitution register status per claimant with the payment reference and date on the same day the payment issues.
Escalate to the Compliance Manager any claim where the remedy is disputed rather than closing it as complete.
checklist.done: every claimant on the register is paid or documented as unlocatable, with a payment reference, letter and dated register entry.

checklist.step: Deliver targeted retraining and supervision changes
actions: Build training that teaches the specific failure the finding names, using de-identified sampled claims as the worked examples.
Assign it in the learning management system to the exact population that handles the affected work, with a completion date ahead of the finding's milestone.
Add a supervisory quality check on the affected step at a defined sampling rate for at least two quarters and report its results into the conduct scorecard.
Attach the completion extract and the first quarter of quality-check results to the finding record.
checklist.done: targeted training is completed by the affected population on time and a two-quarter supervisory check is running and reported.

checklist.step: Report status to the department on the agreed cadence
actions: Prepare the status report on the department's cadence showing per finding: action, milestone status, restitution completed versus owed, and any date at risk.
Disclose a slipping milestone in the report in which it slips, with the revised date and the reason, rather than letting the department discover it at the follow-up exam.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the report and sign it personally before submission.
Record the submission date, the department acknowledgement and any department response against each finding in GRC.
checklist.done: each status report is counsel-cleared, personally signed, submitted on cadence and logged with the department's response.

checklist.step: Commission independent validation before asserting closure
actions: Accept the closure request only when the owner submits the evidence set the plan named, and reject incomplete submissions rather than validating around them.
Direct Internal Audit to test the corrected control on a post-remediation population using the validation method stated in the plan.
Issue a written validation opinion per finding — effective, effective with exceptions, or not remediated — and refuse closure on anything short of effective.
Where the test shows the defect persists, reopen the finding, notify the Head of Compliance the same day and require the department to be told in the next status report.
checklist.done: each finding carries a written independent validation opinion and no finding is closed on anything short of effective.

checklist.step: Close the finding and notify the department
actions: Close the GRC record only with the validation opinion, milestone evidence and completed restitution register attached.
Write the closure notification to the department stating what was done, what was tested, and the restitution total and claimant count, cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
Record the department's acceptance or any follow-up question against the finding, and treat the finding as open until acceptance is received.
Add the finding, its cause and its fix to the prior-findings summary in the exam readiness pack so the next examiner sees a complete history.
checklist.done: the finding is closed on evidence, notified to the department, and carried into the exam readiness prior-findings summary.

checklist.step: Prevent recurrence across the other jurisdictions
actions: For each closed finding assess every other jurisdiction where the same procedure, configuration or team operates and decide whether the same defect exists there.
Where it does, open a self-identified remediation record with the same rigour rather than waiting for that state to examine.
Add a monitoring metric to the quarterly conduct scorecard that would detect recurrence, with a threshold and an owner.
Report the cross-jurisdiction assessment and any self-identified issue to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: every closed finding has a documented cross-jurisdiction assessment, a recurrence metric and any self-identified issue opened.

testing.step: Build the population of open and closed findings
actions: Extract from the GRC platform every market conduct exam finding, settlement agreement obligation and consent order term open at any point in the period, with owner, dates and status.
Reconcile the extract to the final exam reports and settlement agreements themselves, finding by finding, so a finding that was never registered is caught.
Add any regulator commitment made in a status report that does not appear as a GRC record, since undocumented commitments are the ones that get missed.
testing.done: the finding population reconciles line by line to the source reports and agreements, with unregistered commitments added.

testing.step: Reconcile recorded dates to the regulator's own documents
actions: For each finding compare the GRC due dates to the dates stated in the final report, the settlement agreement and the submitted corrective action plan.
Treat any GRC date later than the regulator's date as a control failure in its own right, not a data quality issue.
Confirm the corrective action plan submission date falls inside the window the final report set, and compute the variance in days.
List every date mismatch before sampling begins.
testing.done: every tracked date is reconciled to the regulator's own document and each mismatch is listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of findings
actions: Take 100% of findings closed in the period, 100% of findings involving restitution and 100% of findings that repeat a prior exam issue.
Add 5 open findings at random from a recorded seed to test milestone discipline before closure pressure arrives.
Record population size, seed, draw date and the selected finding numbers in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every closed, restitution-bearing and repeat finding.

testing.step: Re-perform the root cause and affected-population scoping
actions: For each sampled finding read the root cause analysis, then independently query ClaimCenter for claims exposed to the stated cause over the stated period.
Compare your claim count and state coverage to the affected population file and treat an under-scoped population as the most serious exception available, since it caps restitution.
Test specifically whether the population was limited to the examining state where the same procedure or configuration applied elsewhere.
Record your query, count and the variance to the recorded population.
testing.done: each sampled finding has an independently re-scoped affected population with the variance to the company's figure stated.

testing.step: Verify restitution reached the claimants
actions: Sample 40 claimants from the restitution register and trace each to a payment record in ClaimCenter with a payment reference and date.
Recompute the statutory interest for 15 of them from the due date to the payment date at the state's rate and compare to the amount paid.
Confirm the claimant letter explaining the remediation exists in the claim file for each traced claimant.
For unlocatable claimants confirm dated locate attempts and the unclaimed property route, and treat an undocumented write-off as a fail.
testing.done: traced claimants show a payment reference, a recomputed interest figure and an explanatory letter, or a documented unclaimed-property route.

testing.step: Re-perform the corrective control on a post-remediation population
actions: For each sampled closed finding draw 30 claims created after the remediation effective date from the same population the finding concerned.
Test the corrected behaviour directly — the acknowledgement clock now correct for the state, the denial letter now carrying the required provision and DOI block, the diary now firing at 45 days.
Compute the post-remediation error rate and compare it to the examiner's original error rate to show whether the fix actually moved the number.
Treat any recurrence of the original defect as a not-remediated conclusion regardless of the closure paperwork.
testing.done: each closed finding has a post-remediation error rate measured on live claims and compared to the examiner's original rate.

testing.step: Test the closure evidence and validation independence
actions: For each closed finding confirm the GRC record holds the validation opinion, the milestone evidence named in the plan and the completed restitution register.
Confirm the validation opinion is written, dated, states a conclusion and was issued before the closure notification to the department.
Confirm the validator sits outside the Compliance and Claims reporting lines that delivered the action.
Flag any closure asserted to the department before the validation opinion date as a misrepresentation risk and escalate it the same day.
testing.done: every closure carries a dated independent validation opinion issued before the department was told, from a segregated validator.

testing.step: Recompute milestone and reporting timeliness
actions: Build a schedule per finding of every milestone with its regulator-agreed date, actual completion date and the variance in days.
Compute days from draft report receipt to company response against the 30-day window, and days from final report to plan submission against the stated window.
Confirm each status report was submitted on the department's cadence and that any milestone slipping was disclosed in the report of the period in which it slipped.
Present undisclosed slippage separately from late-but-disclosed slippage, because the regulatory consequence differs.
testing.done: every milestone and reporting clock is recomputed in days, with undisclosed slippage identified separately.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the finding, the state, what failed and the exposure it creates with the examining department.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — population under-scoped, cause misdiagnosed, milestone slipped undisclosed, closed without validation, restitution incomplete — and an owner.
Where a closure was asserted to the department on evidence that does not stand up, instruct a corrective notification to the department cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly remediation sweep as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, with unsupported closures routed to a corrective notification.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the proportion of findings closed on validated evidence and the proportion of regulator-agreed dates met, against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — and state ineffective outright where any prior exam finding has repeated.
Sign the workpaper as independent reviewer, having neither owned an action nor delivered a corrective measure.

Report the conclusion, any repeat finding and any corrective notification owed to the department to the Audit Committee and the Compliance Committee, and file the workpaper under 10-year retention in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states closure and on-time rates, a conclusion, any repeat finding, and the committee reporting dates.
